lines: You'd never trust a user ID sent from a browser form. So why trust the one your AI typed?
It's an easy mistake. You give your AI a tool, copy your existing API, so the tool takes a user ID, and you tell the model the user's ID in the prompt. Then the model fills it in.
But the model writes every argument. One wrong guess, or one hostile instruction, and your tool saves to someone else's account.
Getting whose data wrong is real. In 2025, Asana pulled its AI connector for nearly two weeks after finding a bug that could expose data to other organizations.
The fix is the one you already use on the web. The server takes the user from the login, never from the request. The tool just doesn't have a user ID box.
One real memory tool is built this way. Six fields, all filled in by the AI, and which conversation the memory belongs to isn't one of them.
Treat your AI like a browser. Never trust the ID it sends.
facts: Script v5 (Robin, 2026-10-31, on draft 2: 'you had me right up till you described the fix', then 'why is anyone asking the AI who the user is?'; he chose the browser framing). I/VII: the analogy (a tool call's arguments are client input, like a browser form post). II: describes the pattern, not a prevalence claim; mcp-tool-design: chat_id is the required first argument of chat_log_turn and chat_recent on the same server, so models are routinely handed ids to pass. III: where-logic-lives, rules must hold 'if a prompt is missed, the model is confused, or the caller is hostile'; mcp-tool-design, a model has 'decent reason to think' chat_id belongs in write_memory. IV: stakes only, not a claim about Asana's cause (none stated). BleepingComputer and The Register, 2025-06-18: launched May 1, found June 4, offline June 5 to 17; Asana to customers: 'this bug could have potentially exposed certain information from your Asana domain to other Asana MCP users.' V: systems repo storage-routing test (S12): identity and routing come 'from the authenticated context and from nothing a caller supplies'; where-logic-lives: 'server-derived identifiers' at the data-owning boundary. VI: mcp-tool-design: write_memory 'declares six properties and requires all six. chat_id is not among them'; 'chat_id is NOT an input, it is derived server-side from source_turn_id.' Upload description: the two news links and plain devweb.org only (no /articles/ paths, Robin 2026-10-31). Earlier scripts in vo/audition/.
